tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded session logs into Magento admin, opens the Manage Products grid, clicks a row-specific Edit link (for product ID 2766), edits fields on General, Prices, Inventory, and Websites tabs, saves the product, then demonstrates grid filtering and sorting.
- The previous failing tool used a generic wait selector input[type='text'], which did not match any element. This attempt instead interacted with concrete elements (identified by element_hash and indices) and showed that the flow works end-to-end.

Task Definition:
- Purpose: Provide a reusable, deterministic tool that, given product-specific values, will:
  1) Navigate to the Magento admin Manage Products grid (assuming an authenticated session or handling login when redirected).
  2) Open the per-row Edit page for a specific product by navigating directly via its known edit URL id parameter.
  3) Update core product data on the General tab (Name, SKU, Status, Visibility).
  4) Go to the Prices tab and update the Price field.
  5) Go to the Inventory tab and update Qty.
  6) Go to the Websites tab and ensure assignment (Main Website checkbox).
  7) Save the product via the Save button.
  8) Optionally, filter the grid by the updated SKU to verify the change (demonstrated but not essential to the core editing task, so we will omit verification from the core tool steps).
- Core objective for this tool: reliably edit a Magento product’s main fields via the admin UI, using stable element hashes and avoiding generic selectors or brittle waits.

Action Plan:
1) Navigation: Go directly to catalog_product/edit/id/{product_id}/ using a navigation step (this avoids needing to first load the grid and click Edit, and matches the edit_url observed in the logs).
2) General tab edits:
   - Input Name into the Name text field (element_hash df3020a86b).
   - Input SKU into the SKU field (element_hash 1349f1ca81).
   - Change Status select to desired value (Enabled/Disabled) using select_change on element_hash d7baed0536.
   - Change Visibility select to desired value (Not Visible Individually, Catalog, Search, Catalog, Search) using select_change on element_hash 2d6f7788e8.
3) Navigate to Prices tab: click tab link (element_hash 86ed7ee82d).
4) Input Price into the Price field on Prices tab (element_hash e457e89369).
5) Navigate to Inventory tab: click Inventory tab link (element_hash 71d44f34a7).
6) Input Qty in the Qty field on Inventory tab (element_hash 15f8e67c9f).
7) Navigate to Websites tab: click Websites tab link (element_hash 3d30f36949).
8) Ensure product is assigned to Main Website: click the checkbox (element_hash 12bd777a77). Since we don’t know current state, we will treat this as a deterministic click; if the admin consistently wants it checked, they should ensure it is checked after this click (idempotence isn’t guaranteed with a single click).
9) Save product: click the Save button (element_hash 9335489e0b).
10) (Optional verification steps like grid filtering and sorting are omitted to keep tool single-purpose and essential only.)

Variable Identification:
- product_id (string, required): Used in edit URL /admin/catalog_product/edit/id/{product_id}/.
- name (string, required): New product Name for General tab.
- sku (string, required): New SKU value.
- status (string, required, enum ["Enabled","Disabled"]): Status select on General tab.
- visibility (string, required, enum ["Not Visible Individually","Catalog","Search","Catalog, Search"]): Visibility select on General tab.
- price (string, required): Price on Prices tab; Magento accepts decimal as string.
- qty (string, required): Inventory Qty; Magento expects number but we pass as string.
- assign_main_website (bool, optional, default true conceptually): Whether to click the Main Website checkbox on Websites tab. However, the tool step will always click; we model this as a bool mainly for documentation. Because the step sequence must be unconditional, we won’t branch, but we can still expose this parameter to allow other tools to ignore it; the actual click is essential to demonstrate Websites interaction as per task, so we keep it.

Step Optimization:
- We skip logging in explicitly: Magento will redirect unauthenticated requests to the login form, and prior tools already contain stable login interactions. For this task we assume the agent is logged in, as allowed by the instructions.
- We navigate directly to the edit URL using product_id instead of loading grid and selecting Edit. This is faster and less brittle while still using the same backend route the grid uses.
- We avoid any generic selectors such as input[type='text'] and instead rely on element_hash values captured for the specific controls.
- We omit grid filtering and sorting from the core tool because they are not required to complete the product edit itself and would add non-essential complexity.
- No explicit wait steps are necessary in this definition format; robustness should be handled by the underlying controller using elementHash-based resolution.

This tool therefore focuses strictly on editing a single product’s core fields and saving it, using deterministic navigation and interactions.
name: tool_edit_product_magento_admin_v5
description: Open a specific product edit page from the Magento 1.x admin Manage Products grid, update key fields (name, SKU, status, visibility, price, inventory quantity, website assignment) and save the product, using robust selectors and avoiding generic input[type='text'] waits.

steps.description: Open the Magento admin product edit page for the specified product ID using its direct edit URL.
Set the General tab Name field to the provided product name.
Set the General tab SKU field to the provided SKU value.
Set the General tab Status dropdown to the desired status (Enabled/Disabled).
Set the General tab Visibility dropdown to the desired visibility option.
Open the Prices tab in the Product Information side navigation.
Set the Prices tab Price field to the provided price value.
Open the Inventory tab in the Product Information side navigation.
Set the Inventory tab Qty field to the provided inventory quantity.
Open the Websites tab in the Product Information side navigation.
Toggle assignment of the product to Main Website via the checkbox on the Websites tab (typically to ensure it is assigned).
Save the product with the updated fields using the Save button.

input_schema.name: product_id
input_schema.description: Numeric Magento product entity ID used in the edit URL /admin/catalog_product/edit/id/{product_id}/.

input_schema.name: name
input_schema.description: New Name value for the product on the General tab (Name * field, STORE VIEW scope).

input_schema.name: sku
input_schema.description: New SKU value for the product on the General tab (SKU * field, GLOBAL scope).

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: Product Status on the General tab. Allowed values: Enabled or Disabled.

input_schema.name: visibility
input_schema.description: Product Visibility on the General tab. Choose how the product is shown in frontend catalog/search.

input_schema.name: price
input_schema.description: Product Price value (in store currency, e.g., 47.50) on the Prices tab (Price * field).

input_schema.name: qty
input_schema.description: Inventory quantity for the product on the Inventory tab (Qty * field).

input_schema.name: assign_main_website
input_schema.description: Whether to ensure the product is assigned to Main Website by clicking the Main Website checkbox on the Websites tab. The tool will always click the checkbox as part of the Websites interaction.
